query: tell me more about the Spotify protest
search_query: Spotify protest Hotline TNT King Gizzard defense companies
answer:
The protest began in **June 2025** when indie‑rock quartet **Deerhoof** announced that they were pulling their catalog from Spotify. Within weeks, other acts—including **Xiu Xiu**, **King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard** and **Hotline TNT**—followed suit, and the exodus continued into **September** with groups such as **The Mynabirds**, **WU LYF**, **Kadhja Bonet** and **Young Widows** also leaving the platform [1].

All of the bands cited the same trigger: **Spotify CEO Daniel Ek’s investment fund, Prima Materia, has been funding the defense company Helsing**, which develops artificial‑intelligence software that informs military decisions [2][4]. The artists argue that Spotify’s financial ties to a war‑related firm are incompatible with their values. In a statement, Hotline TNT’s frontman Will Anderson wrote, “The company that bills itself as the steward of all recorded music has proven beyond the shadow of a doubt that it does not align with the band's values in any way” [2][5].

The protest has grown to include a wide range of musicians. In addition to the groups above, **Godspeed You! Black Emperor**, **Massive Attack** and **Sylvan Esso** have also removed their music from Spotify, while **Deerhoof, Xiu Xiu, King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, Godspeed You! Black Emperor, Hotline TNT, Massive Attack, and Sylvan Esso** all cited concerns over Ek’s investment in Helsing [4]. Some artists have taken the boycott further by pulling their catalog from all major streaming services, not just Spotify [2].

While the music remains available on other platforms such as **Bandcamp**, the collective action has drawn attention to Spotify’s broader controversies, including its handling of AI‑generated music and alleged “ghost artist” schemes that reduce payments to real musicians [5]. The protest has become a prominent example of artists using their platform to challenge corporate practices that conflict with their ethical positions.

sources.title: All the artists leaving Spotify | The FADER
sources.snippet:
On July 25, Australian band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard took to Instagram to announce that they pulled their music from Spotify. They were the latest group to abandon the platform in the wake of reports that Spotify CEO and co-founder Daniel Ek secured millions for defense company Helsing through his investment fund, Prima Materia.

ADVERTISEMENT [...] The news has led to backlash against Spotify, which has already been the subject of numerous controversies in the past year, including its platforming of AI music and reported “ghost artist” schemes that decrease the money paid to real artists.

Here are all the groups who have decided to boycott the platform.
